scope: The minimal positive quadratic Q-regularizer for K1359's repository-owned operator-charge scalar electrodynamics, selected backward from K1364's exact coercivity demand; not a source-selected action term, compact generator or observed charge law.

regularized_action.action_convention: Add -mu||Q phi||^2 to the Lorentzian Lagrangian and +mu||Q phi||^2 to the conserved classical energy.
regularized_action.local_gauge_identity: Q exp(i alpha Q)phi=exp(i alpha Q)Qphi
regularized_action.local_gauge_invariance: V_Q(exp(i alpha Q)phi)=V_Q(phi) pointwise for every real local alpha.
regularized_action.euler_contribution: The closed-form derivative contributes mu Q^2 phi to the strong matter equation on D(Q^2).
regularized_action.brst_invariance: s V_Q=0 on the common core because s phi=i c Q phi, Q is self-adjoint and the infinitesimal circle action is unitary.

coercivity.k1364_sequence: For phi_N=sum_(n<=N)n^-1 e_(4n), the added term equals 16 mu N and therefore removes the bounded-energy escape exactly.
coercivity.spatial_limit: The bound controls the internal charge graph term. Ordinary H1 control from the covariant gradient additionally requires an admissible gauge/spatial estimate; it is not inferred from this term alone.

claim_ceiling: Adding the repository-owned term mu||Q phi||^2 with mu>0 is exactly local-circle-gauge and BRST invariant on the common core and makes the classical energy coercive in the internal charge graph norm. It repairs K1364's counterexample but neither derives Q or mu from the source nor proves spatial H1 control or global nonlinear coupled evolution.
